memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Joshua set up the twelve stones that had been in the middle of the Jordan at the spot where the priests who carried the ark of the covenant had stood. And they are there to this day. — Josh 4:9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
There is a second memorial here, easy to miss. Alongside the twelve stones carried out to the camp, Joshua also set up stones in the middle of the Jordan itself, right where the priests had stood holding the ark. When the waters returned, these stones would be hidden beneath the river, unseen — but still there.

That is a striking picture. One memorial stood in plain view at Gilgal for all to see; another lay quietly beneath the waters, known but hidden. Both marked the same great act of God. Not every testimony to God's faithfulness is public. Some of what God does in our lives is known only to Him and to us, hidden beneath the surface, yet no less real.

The phrase "they are there to this day" tells us this was written down later, as a settled fact. God's works leave a lasting mark. What He does does not simply vanish; it endures.

There is comfort here for the believer whose deepest experiences of God are private and unseen by others. God sees. He knows the hidden stones in the riverbed of your life — the quiet answered prayers, the private struggles He carried you through. Nothing done in Him is ever wasted or forgotten. Our lives are hidden with Christ in God (Col 3:3), and every hidden work of grace is fully known to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What "hidden stones" of God's faithfulness has He placed in your life that only you know?
2. Are you content when some of your walk with God stays private and unseen?
3. How does it comfort you that God sees and remembers the hidden things?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You see even the hidden works of grace in my life. Help me trust that nothing done in You is ever forgotten. Amen.
